questions.question: How do you prioritize features when resources and time are limited?
questions.ideal_answer: Use a structured prioritization framework such as RICE (Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort) or MoSCoW (Must-have, Should-have, Could-have, Won't-have). Align priorities with company strategic goals, user feedback, and ROI. Involve engineering and design early to estimate effort and trade-offs accurately.
key_points: Uses established prioritization frameworks (RICE, Eisenhower, MoSCoW)
Aligns feature backlog with business goals and user impact
Validates assumptions with quantitative and qualitative data
Communicates prioritization decisions transparently to stakeholders

questions.question: How do you define success metrics for a new product feature?
questions.ideal_answer: Define primary North Star metric and supporting input metrics (adoption, engagement, retention, monetization, CSAT). Differentiate between vanity metrics and actionable metrics. Define counter-metrics to ensure the new feature doesn't harm core user experience or performance.
key_points: Identifies North Star metric aligned with product goal
Breaks down metrics into adoption, engagement, and retention
Defines counter-metrics to monitor unintended negative impacts
Uses A/B testing or cohort analysis for measurement
